themes.theme: ai driven capex and semiconductor demand
themes.consensus_view: Banks broadly agree AI infrastructure spending and memory-chip demand are driving an earnings boom, but a vocal minority warns the AI-linked stocks have run too far and crowded positioning is starting to unwind.

facts_agreed.claim: Hyperscaler AI capex and advance orders are driving a structural surge in demand for semiconductors and AI infrastructure.
evidence_quotes: NVDA’s $124bn purchase commitment suggests robust demand/supply visibility ahead for AI infra.
hyperscalers’ USD 2tr worth of advance orders in compute resources further illustrates this trend
earnings growth, boosted by AI capex spend
A key catalyst for this strength is the capex boom underway
AI is turning memory into a structural bottleneck.
If history repeats, payrolls revisions should start improving in line with the jump in earnings expectations.

facts_agreed.claim: The memory and semiconductor cycle is supply-constrained, supporting prices and earnings for chipmakers.
evidence_quotes: DRAM/NAND/HBM cycles to expand memory valuation multiples
the whole cycle is supply side constrained by the length of time
This is not a normal cyclical upswing; it is a structural reset
sales continue to grow at a much faster pace than inventories

facts_agreed.claim: AI capex is a primary driver of US growth and equity-market leadership in the current regime.
evidence_quotes: shift from capital light equity market leadership, to the new capex intensive regime
GIR expect AI to boost true capex growth by 3.3pp in 2026
If history repeats, payrolls revisions should start improving in line with the jump in earnings expectations.

facts_contested.claim: Whether AI-linked equity valuations and positioning are sustainable or set up for a violent unwind
facts_contested.for_evidence: NVDA’s $124bn purchase commitment suggests robust demand/supply visibility ahead for AI infra.
facts_contested.against_evidence: crowded positioning, leverage, and AI momentum worked together. Today they all started moving in reverse.

facts_contested.claim: Whether all incremental AI compute will be absorbed by frontier data centers or partly run on older hardware
facts_contested.for_evidence: hyperscalers’ USD 2tr worth of advance orders in compute resources further illustrates this trend
facts_contested.against_evidence: The world will always have a place for the frontier, but to think it will consume the majority of tokens feels irrational.

themes.consensus_view: Banks agree the US labor market and broader economy stayed surprisingly strong through May, with the 172k payroll print well above the ~85k consensus reinforcing a resilient backdrop for stocks and consumer spending.

facts_agreed.claim: US job growth came in well above expectations in May, signaling continued labor-market resilience.
evidence_quotes: job growth has turned positive again, after a (non-recessionary) weak patch
Employment growth continues to exceed forecasts, supporting the impression of a surprisingly robust US economy.
All in all, economic resilience remains.

facts_agreed.claim: A stable labor market is keeping US consumers spending despite real income pressure.
evidence_quotes: the “no fire” part of the US “no hire, no fire” labor market is reassuring consumers

facts_agreed.claim: AI is a secular growth driver that supports US economic and earnings strength even through cyclical wobbles.
evidence_quotes: AI revolution was going to kick off, providing a secular growth driver
AI will not obsolete the human brain.

themes.consensus_view: Banks across 12 desks flag the Iran/Middle East conflict as a live driver of energy prices and headline inflation, but none stake a directional call on where oil settles from here.

facts_agreed.claim: Multiple banks reference the Iran/Middle East conflict as a near-term shock to energy prices and inflation without staking a directional view.
evidence_quotes: Iran war impact on energy prices
War in Iran energy cost impact
Middle East conflict as global energy shock
Middle East tensions driving oil prices
Brent oil supply disruption risk
Middle East conflict shipment delays
Iran war energy-driven inflation spike

themes.consensus_view: Banks across more than a dozen desks reference the Strait of Hormuz situation and potential normalization of shipping as a live macro variable, but only one has staked a directional view that reopening would support markets.

facts_agreed.claim: Multiple banks flag the Strait of Hormuz situation and potential normalization of energy flows and shipping as an active near-term macro topic.
evidence_quotes: potential normalisation of maritime trade through the Strait, combined with the positive tone
Strait of Hormuz traffic normalization
Strait of Hormuz reopening
Strait of Hormuz trade flow recovery
Persian Gulf de-escalation
Strait of Hormuz shipping normalization

themes.consensus_view: Banks expect the European Central Bank to raise its deposit rate by a quarter-point (0.25 percentage points) at the June 11 meeting, with most pointing to energy-driven inflation risk as the reason.

facts_agreed.claim: The ECB is expected to deliver a 25 basis point (0.25 percentage point) hike to the deposit rate at its upcoming meeting.
evidence_quotes: We expect the Governing Council to raise the deposit rate by 25bp
we see a final rate increase in September, bringing the deposit rate to 2.50%
Inflationary risks from higher energy prices will result in a pre-emptive rate hike by 25 bp.
The European Central Bank is priced for lift-off with a 25bps hike on Thursday.

themes.consensus_view: Banks broadly agree that leveraged ETFs and options flows are now a dominant force in price formation, with positioning at extremes that makes the market more vulnerable to sharp reversals.

facts_agreed.claim: Leveraged and inverse ETFs have grown large enough to drive market momentum and amplify price swings.
evidence_quotes: The recent growth of levered ETF AUM + trading volumes in the products has been staggering
leveraged ETF rebalancing
Short gamma effect in levered ETFs

facts_agreed.claim: Options flows and gamma dynamics now play a bigger role in shaping equity price action than they did historically.
evidence_quotes: Price action is increasingly being shaped by gamma and other options-related flows
Retail gambling in 0DTE options and leveraged ETFs
Short gamma effect in levered ETFs

facts_agreed.claim: Market positioning has swung to risk-on extremes that look stretched.
evidence_quotes: risk has swung from despair to exuberance
Stocks are bounding ever higher, but this is increasingly being fueled by the destabilising force of leverage.

themes.consensus_view: Seven banks flag the Fed's pre-FOMC quiet period as a near-term backdrop heading into the June meeting, but none stakes a directional view on what it means for markets.

Fed blackout window
